newsitem.title: UK: British Midland Q1 cargo volumes, revenues rise.
newsitem.headline: British Midland Q1 cargo volumes, revenues rise.

text.p: British Midland carried 5,226 tonnes of cargo in January-March this year, up 8.4 percent on the 4,817 tonnes flown in the same period in 1996, said cargo marketing manager Louise Shenton.
She told Reuters that these totals covered the carrier's Cargo, Priority and Roadlink volumes carried but excluded mail.
She added that revenues earned during the first quarter were up 14 percent on January-March 1996 but she declined to give details.
The carrier said last year that it earned 6.7 million stg in scheduled cargo revenues in 1995.
Shenton said this total increased by 10.4 percent last year to 7.4 million stg.
In 1995, the airline carried some 11,000 tonnes of cargo and 12,100 tonnes in 1996.

Cargo manager Terry Greetham added that British Midland's UK cargo wholesaling sister company, International Cargo Marketing (ICM), had achieved a first quarter revenue increase of 40 percent on the same period last year but also declined to detail figures.
"For both companies, we have seen the exceptional growth achieved in the last quarter of 1996 continue this year," he said.

"It is difficult to explain exactly why but two factors that have helped our performance have been further concentration on the (high-yield) express end of the market and improving our customer service levels," he said.
-Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
